name: Render: Layered Layout Demo
description: Demonstrates layering, positioning, and sizing by rendering multiple impulses with different position modes and z-index layers. Shows center overlays, absolute positioning, and flow content side-by-side.

tasks.description: Render the base content layer (flow, layer 0).

prompt.template:
Render the base layer of a layered layout demo.

Use render_ui to push a grid dashboard as the background content:
- primitive.type: container
- primitive.layout: grid
- primitive.columns: 2
- primitive.gap: 16
- primitive.padding: 24
- primitive.children: 4 cards (each a vertical naked container with a heading and some content)
- position.mode: flow
- animation: fade
- No layer property (defaults to 0)

Make the 4 cards: 'Active Sessions (127)', 'Request Rate (2.3k/s)', 'Error Rate (0.4%)', 'Cache Hit (94%)'.
Each card: naked container, gap 8, padding 16, background #f9fafb, borderRadius 8
  - text heading with the metric name
  - progress bar showing an appropriate value
  - text caption with a brief explanation

Call render_ui once.

tasks.description: Render a centered overlay on top (layer 10).

prompt.template:
The previous task rendered a grid dashboard as the base layer.

Now render a notification overlay using render_ui:
- primitive.type: container
- primitive.layout: vertical
- primitive.gap: 12
- primitive.padding: 24
- primitive.maxWidth: 400
- primitive.background: #ffffff
- primitive.borderRadius: 12
- primitive.naked: true
- primitive.children:
  1. A horizontal naked container with a badge (variant: warning, text: 'Alert') and a text heading 'Deployment in Progress'
  2. A progress bar (type: bar, value: 67, label: 'Step 2 of 3')
  3. A text body 'API service rolling update — 4 of 6 instances updated'
  4. A horizontal naked container (gap: 8) with two buttons: 'View Details' (variant: primary, onClick: view-details) and 'Dismiss' (variant: ghost, onClick: dismiss)
- position.mode: center
- animation: scale
- layer: 10

This will appear as a centered modal overlay on top of the dashboard.
Call render_ui once.
